So we are all aware of this force which pulls us all towards the centre of our planet, called gravity. Good.

Now imagine you are flying an aeroplane and you have a nice cup of hot coffee sat on a tray in front of you. At some point aircraft begins to turn, which essentially means pointing one of it's wings towards the ground. Why does the liquid in my cup stay level? What forces offset gravity trying to spill my coffee?
Why does my coffee not spill on a plane?
Centrifugal Force, similar as if you were to put your coffee on this thing and spin it around in a circle. As an airplane banks and turns, the G-forces created by the turn keep the coffee level.

That makes sense, thank you. Would it however be possible to create a scenario where the coffee does in fact spill? I guess my question is whether it is possible to bank the plane without changing the direction of flight - in which case there would be no G force generated by the turn itself to offset gravity.

Absolutely - however airline pilots (and actually all pilots) spend a lot of time keeping the center of gravity centered during flight manuevers. You can roll an airplane while keep the direction of travel straight relatively easily. Read this article for more information on the axis of flight in relation to the center of gravity.

Not a computer specialist. I have a question. What would installing a Win10 update to a Win7 machine actually do?

If you mean trying to install a patch meant for Windows 10 onto Windows 7: Absolutely nothing. The Windows Installer would refuse to run it.

Even if you could somehow "trick" it into doing so, Windows' file protection might just revert the changes, since those files were not meant for your OS. Not sure if it goes by just digital signature, or if it checks file versions. (All Win 10 OS files would have a different version in their metadata. If you tried to modify the version metadata, file protection would certainly erase them, because you'd break the digital signature in the process)

If you mean running the Windows 10 update installation on a Win 7 machine, then all it does is shove Win7 off to the side into a backup folder (So you can restore back to Win7, or so that the installer can revert back to your original configuration if something gets fucked up in the middle of the install), install Win10, then move your settings over.

This isn't bricking, but it is annoying and serious. It isn't an if, but a when. Micrsoft will release something that WILL brick machines because of some vague conflict error that slipped through the cracks. There are millions of possible combinations of hardware and software, there simply is no way to cover them all. Mandatory installs and reboots would SEEM like a good idea, but reality is a different matter.
And this is why I'm sticking with Windows 7 for the next few months.
